headline: Two former army officers arrested in Dhaka under anti-terrorism and cyber security laws
summary: Lieutenant Colonel (retd.) Debashish and Lieutenant (retd.) Gulshan Ara were apprehended in connection with cases filed under the Anti-Terrorism and Cyber Security Acts.
details: Two former army officers, Lieutenant Colonel (retd.) Debashish and Lieutenant (retd.) Gulshan Ara, have been arrested in Dhaka. They were apprehended in connection with cases filed under the Anti-Terrorism and Cyber Security Acts.
Md. Shafiqul Islam, Additional Commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Detective Branch, confirmed their arrests this Monday morning following an operation in the capital.
A source revealed that former army officer Debashish was arrested due to his alleged association with Gulshan Ara, who is an accused in cases under the Anti-Terrorism and Cyber Security Acts.
caption:
Two retired army officers, including a Lieutenant Colonel, have been arrested in Dhaka under anti-terrorism and cyber security laws.

Two former army officers, Lieutenant Colonel (retd.) Debashish and Lieutenant (retd.) Gulshan Ara, have been arrested in Dhaka. They were apprehended in connection with cases filed under the Anti-Terrorism and Cyber Security Acts.

Md. Shafiqul Islam, Additional Commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Detective Branch, confirmed their arrests this Monday morning following an operation in the capital.

A source revealed that former army officer Debashish was arrested due to his alleged association with Gulshan Ara, who is an accused in cases under the Anti-Terrorism and Cyber Security Acts.

headline_marked: [[2 Bangladeshis killed, 24 injured]] in Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport
headline: 2 Bangladeshis killed, 24 injured in Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport
summary: Houthi rebels launched fresh strikes on Riyadh's international airport, following a previous attack that killed 12 people and injured hundreds, including Bangladeshis. Operations at the airport have been suspended.
details: A series of Houthi strikes have targeted Riyadh's international airport, resulting in significant casualties and property damage. Among the victims, two Bangladeshis were killed and 24 others were injured in the attacks, which have escalated the conflict in Yemen.

The Iran-backed Houthi group claimed responsibility for multiple attacks over the past 24 hours, including on the airport, and vowed to continue targeting Saudi Arabia's transit hubs. They described these locations as "a theatre of operations for our forces."

On Sunday, a projectile struck King Khalid International Airport, causing a fire and wounding 11 people, including one Pakistani resident who died. Saudi air defenses also intercepted a missile nearby. The airport's closure was extended by 24 hours.

Saturday's attack, described as the deadliest on Saudi soil in over a decade, killed 12 people and wounded 309. Nationalities of the deceased included four Saudis, two Bangladeshis, one American, one Egyptian, one Jordanian, one Syrian, one Palestinian, and one Sudanese.

The attacks drew widespread international condemnation from the United Nations and world leaders, including US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The anti-Houthi coalition labeled Saturday's attack a "full-fledged war crime" and pledged a decisive response.

Despite Saudi Arabia's substantial military investment, Houthi attacks continue to penetrate its defenses. Security analysts note the vast size of Saudi Arabia makes consistent defense against such attacks challenging.

The airport strikes occurred on the eve of Saudi Arabia's high-profile convention and entertainment season, and also at the start of the peak travel season for Umrah pilgrims, affecting millions of Muslims globally.
